decisions.statement: The change to run is handed in by the caller rather than read off the call.
A change is reached by its address rather than by a name held here.
A word naming no change is refused by that word rather than by an address.
A word near a change's name is refused with that name pointed at.
The change is loaded before the turn over the edits is taken.
The arguments a change takes are read from standard input.
A call piping nothing in is refused rather than run with no argument.
That refusal names the arguments the change named takes.
The help flag piped in as the whole body is answered rather than refused.
That answer is the change's definition and the arguments that change takes.
The arguments a change takes are read off the change rather than off its page.
A word naming no change is refused before what is piped in is read.
The key `at` names a path.
A path is read against the repository root here rather than by the change.
A path is read with the whitespace at either end taken off.
A path running over more than one line is refused before the change is loaded.
A path outside the repository is refused before the change is loaded.
A path under the folder git does not track is refused before the change is loaded.
Every change is refused that path here rather than each change refusing it.
Every other value with a quote or a newline reaches the change as the caller wrote it.
The value at `message` says what the commit is for.
The key `message` is read here rather than handed to the change.
An empty `message` is refused before the change is loaded.
The key `draft` keeps the edits for a later apply rather than applying.
`draft` takes `true` or `false` and no other value.
`draft` beside `message` is refused before the change is loaded.
The key `draft` is read here rather than handed to the change.
The key `measure` measures the landing the change reaches.
`measure` takes `true` and no other value.
`measure` beside `draft` is refused before the change is loaded.
The key `measure` is read here rather than handed to the change.
A caller settling what a run does with its edits bars the keys saying otherwise.
The call as it was made is handed in by the caller rather than spelled here.
A run keeping its edits names where they are kept and the apply landing them.
A run names its edits on the list it is handed as soon as those edits are appended.
A run appending no edit names nothing on that list.
A run whose change answered no edit says that change answered none.
The edits a change answers are appended beside the calling agent's page.
Every edit appended carries whether the readers of that path owe the reading again.
That answer is read off the change kind the change's page names.
A change reaches its kind whether or not it names that kind's page type.
A change page reaching nothing leaves the readers of every path owing the reading.
An agent whose page is nowhere is refused rather than answered with nothing.
That refusal is worded where every act over the edits kept reads it.
Two runs leave two sets of edits in the order the runs were made.
A change is handed the world the edits appended before that change leave.
The edits appended before are folded into one answer to work that world out.
A fold that refuses refuses the run rather than being read as an empty world.
A fold that refuses is a fault of the data.
A change that refuses appends nothing and says why the change refused.
A change that refuses is a fault of what the call was handed.
A change that threw is an operational fault.
A turn over the edits kept that would not open is an operational fault.
Every answer here is built by a function rather than written out as a value.
A world whose shadow will not build refuses the run.
A path a folder sits at holds no body.
A change reads that path as empty.
The edits are read and appended to under one turn over the file the edits fill.
No check runs over the change itself.
What one run of one change cost is appended beside the page the caller names.
The cost is taken around the change rather than around the apply that follows.
A run refused before the change is reached is recorded nowhere.
A change whose writer owes reading is refused before that change's edits are appended.
The reading a writer owes is asked for at the change rather than at the apply.
A change whose writer owes no reading is passed over by that warrant.
The reading a change owes is the reading that change's own edits owe.
An edit kept before is owed nothing again by the change drafted after it.
The world those edits leave is still what the warrants are worked out against.
A change that refuses applies nothing and lands nothing.
A change that refuses writes no body onto the tree.
An apply lands every edit kept rather than the edits that run appended.
A call that applied says nothing of the edits being kept for a later apply.
An apply that refuses leaves the edits kept and names what lands them.
A call naming no change is refused with every change the index has.
A change is run under the processor seconds that change's page allows.
A change past those seconds runs to its end and then appends nothing.
Those seconds are taken around the change alone rather than around the whole call.

definition: one mechanical change run for the edits it answers
